web_evidence.title: The Nest — By Cynthia D'Aprix Sweeney
web_evidence.note: Authorized pre-publication excerpt, used with Ecco’s permission, sustains third-person narration through Leo and Matilda and accesses both characters’ perceptions and thoughts.

web_evidence.title: The Nest Reading Guide
web_evidence.note: The book’s reading guide explicitly describes the novel as structured through multiple characters’ perspectives and in the third person.

web_evidence.title: Cynthia D'Aprix Sweeney Writing Styles in The Nest

web_evidence.title: Ellie Kemper on The Nest: “I Could Not Put This Book Down”
web_evidence.note: The review describes the novel’s continuous rotation among character viewpoints, corroborating the multi-focal structure shown by the third-person evidence.

person_note: The Goodreads passages repeatedly present several characters externally as she/he while entering their private beliefs, memories, and wishes; dialogue and aphoristic uses of I or you are local rather than competing base narration. The authorized opening independently sustains the same third-person mode across Leo and Matilda, while the whole-book reading guide explicitly states that the multiple character perspectives are in third person; the study guide corroborates third-person omniscience. Rotating focal characters therefore do not constitute person alternation. No credible evidence of sustained first- or second-person base sections was found; remaining uncertainty is limited to the incomplete scope of the authorized excerpt, resolved by the explicit whole-book structural sources.
